content.thinking:
I'm drafting the postmortem now, starting with the symptom: shoppers' account pages were showing spend totals that lagged behind their purchases. The alert says the cached figures disagree with the ledger, and the cached pages are what show the frozen numbers, so I'm working out how the stale data reached the pages.

I'm laying out the causal chain for the postmortem: account pages showed spend totals behind shoppers' purchases, and the cached spend entries stopped updating from the purchase ledger at A5. I still don't know why the cache stopped updating. The records I've read show no deploy or flag change on io-shop, but the windows I checked don't all cover the time of the failure.

I'm weighing whether the missing read-side check is the root cause or just the reason the stale figures reached the page. Since the cache stopping its updates is what set this off and that's still unexplained, I'm leaning toward treating the unchecked cache reads as a contributing factor.

I'm settling on the mechanism for the postmortem: the page served cached entries without checking they still covered the shopper's purchases, so once the updates stopped, the frozen figures reached the page. Since the cache stopping is what set this off and its cause is still unknown, I'm treating that missing read-side check as a contributing factor rather than the root cause.

I'm settling the root cause for the postmortem: whatever keeps the cached spend totals current stopped updating them from the purchase ledger at A5, leaving each figure frozen while purchases kept coming in. The evidence I've read doesn't show why the updates stopped, and no deploy or flag change turned up in the windows I checked, so I'm marking that as not yet reached.

I'm settling the chain for the postmortem: the first step is what shoppers saw, the account pages showing spend totals behind their purchases, and the next is that the cached copies stopped keeping up with the ledger at A5. The step after that, the reason the cache stopped updating, is one the record doesn't show, so the chain stops there.

I'm settling the second step of the chain: the pages were reading from cached copies that had stopped keeping up with the purchase ledger from A5, while the ledger itself stayed correct. Nothing earlier in the record shows a change that set this off, and the only thing I've ruled out so far is a flag change.

I'm checking whether any deploy or flag change on io-shop shows up in the windows I read, and none does, though the hour before 20:54 doesn't reach back to the 17:56 onset. I'm treating that as the absence of a recorded change rather than proof one was ruled out, and I still need to note that the reason the updates stopped isn't shown in the evidence.

I'm noting the mitigation: the store reported what it removed, which accounts for the wrong figures, but nothing is refreshing the cached copies, so any cached figure will go stale again when its shopper buys, and pages will keep showing it until the feed resumes or the fix is merged. I'm starting the contributing factors list with the account page's use of any cached spend entry without a check.

I'm adding the second contributing factor: no alert caught the cache updates stopping, and the stale figures were only found by the staleness check well after A5.

I'm working out the remaining contributing factors for the postmortem: the alert only caught the stale figures well after the cache stopped updating, and nothing paged anyone at the time, which I'll record as its own finding. I'm also weighing whether the missing metrics and logs belong in the contributing factors, since they meant the impact couldn't be measured directly.

I'm weighing whether the cache's own feed is the thing to check next, since changes to it weren't in the record I read. The contributing factors are the main thing left, and I'm considering whether the thin metrics and logs belong among them or only as an action item to make them readable.

I'm turning to the action items now: one to find out why whatever updates io-summary-cache's spend entries stopped from A5, owned by checkout-platform, and another to restart those updates and confirm the entries track the ledger again.

I'm moving on to what went well: the mitigation agent discarded the 90 stale figures and confirmed the result, and the investigator's wide read of the change history is worth recording as its own item. I'm also weighing how to note Code-Fix's draft PR #445 without saying what it does, and whether to mark the open question of why the cache feed stopped as unresolved.

I'm settling the last points for the postmortem: the cause and assumptions. I'm noting that the onset is taken from A5, the point where the alert dated the cached copies stopping, and that I'm inferring the pages read cached figures from the record, without having confirmed the file reading.

I'm settling the wording for the cause in plain words: the saved spending totals stopped being brought up to date while the purchase record stayed correct, and the account pages likely showed those saved copies without checking they were current, though the record doesn't show why the updating stopped. For the root cause, I'm stating that the entries in io-summary-cache stopped being updated from the purchase ledger at A5, so each one froze and fell behind when its shopper bought again. For the symptom, I'm keeping it to shoppers seeing spend totals that were missing their latest purchases. Next I'm turning to what went wrong, starting with the fact that nobody was paged.

I'm weighing the "whole of what was wrong" line from the mitigation verdict against the alert's note that nothing was restoring the copies, so I'm treating it as a possible went-wrong item. Then I'm sketching the action items: find out why the cache entries stopped updating from A5, restore the updates, add an alert for entries that stop refreshing, and route the stale-data check to an on-call page, with the last one possibly tied to the second contributing factor.

I'm mapping the remaining follow-up items to their contributing factors and checking which evidence backs each step of the causal chain. The first step rests on the alert's note, and the second adds the cache-feed change to be checked. For the deploy and flag checks, I'm noting that changes to io-summary-cache and its feed were never read, so those are open rather than ruled out.

I'm weighing whether the missing metrics belong in the contributing factors or only as an action item, and I'm leaning toward keeping them as an action item since the stale copies wouldn't have been caught by better metrics alone. For the mitigation point, I'll note the discarded figures without treating them as the whole fix, and I'll leave the open question of why the cache feed stopped marked as unresolved.

action_items.item: checkout-platform to find out why the spend entries in io-summary-cache stopped being updated from the purchase ledger from {A5}.
Restore the updates that keep io-summary-cache's spend entries in step with the purchase ledger.
Add an alert that fires when io-summary-cache's spend entries stop being updated from the purchase ledger, separate from the check comparing figures with purchases.
Route CachedSpendTotalsAreStale on io-shop to the on-call rotation so a person is paged when it fires.
Make io-shop's per-minute metrics and log lines readable to the investigation, since none came back for this incident.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account pages showed cached spend figures that left out purchases the purchase ledger had already recorded correctly.

ruled_out.what: A deploy or release on io-shop: no production changes came back from either window read, which together cover the time the copies stopped keeping up.
A flag change on io-shop by anyone but Argus: the flag provider's history showed none in the hour it read.

causal_chain.step: The account pages read those figures from cached copies in io-summary-cache, and the copies had stopped keeping up with the purchase ledger from {A5}, the oldest purchase none of the stale copies accounted for, so each copy froze and went stale again whenever its shopper bought. Why the updates stopped is not shown: no change on io-shop came back from the windows read, and changes to io-summary-cache or whatever feeds it were not seen in the record, so nothing found here was either tied to the stop or ruled out by a healthy measurement.

input.cause_in_plain_words: The saved copies of shoppers' spending totals stopped being brought up to date while the record of their purchases stayed correct, and the account pages likely showed those saved copies without checking they were still current; the record does not show why the updating stopped.

contributing_factors.factor: In the files Code-Fix read, the account page used any cached spend entry the cache gave back without checking that the entry still covered the shopper's purchases, even though each entry stores how many purchases it was worked out over and the page already holds the shopper's purchases (F1).
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: With the cache still stalled, the page would have treated each behind entry as a miss and worked the figure out from the correct ledger, so shoppers would not have seen stale totals.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No alert was seen on the cache updates stopping: the stale copies were found only by the check comparing cached figures with the purchases behind them, which fired {alert_raised - A5} after the copies stopped keeping up.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: An alert on the updates stopping would have caught the stall as it began, before shoppers bought again and their pages fell behind.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent read io-shop's production changes over two windows that together reach well back before the copies stopped keeping up, and the flag provider's history was read as well, so no deploy or flag change on the service was left unchecked.
The Mitigation Agent discarded the stale cached figures of io-shop, sending those pages back to the correct purchase ledger, and the action was judged confirmed with nothing to put back.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request #445 for a person to review.

went_wrong: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.
Argus moved the incident to MITIGATED calling the discarded entries the whole of what was wrong, while the alert itself said nothing was putting the copies right and later checks would name more.

input.root_cause: The cached spend entries in io-summary-cache stopped being updated from the purchase ledger from {A5}, so each entry kept its last value and fell further behind every time its shopper bought again, while the ledger itself stayed correct; nothing the record read shows why the updates stopped.
input.still_at_risk: Any cached spend figure could go stale again as soon as its shopper bought again, and account pages could show it until the cache updates are restored or a check on the read side is in place.
input.symptom: Account pages showed shoppers spend totals missing their latest purchases
